title: Personal information · Detail and inference
learn: A detail is stated; an inference combines clues to reach a supported conclusion. Separate a reasonable inference from a guess. For example, a request for a later slot may suggest a timing difficulty, but does not prove what caused it. State the clues and qualify uncertain conclusions.
guided_practice: Use the first checked task to practise the rule or strategy. Read its explanation, correct an error and explain why the answer fits. For the productive tasks, compare your response with the example and rubric before revising.
key_language: record, reference card, because, confirm, support
learner_material:
A SHORT ACCOUNT
I moved to a new flat last week. I wrote down my new address and checked the postcode. Later, I spoke to Amina at Park Learning Centre. We arranged a information session for Monday 04 January 2027 at 10:30. Finally, I copied the reference BE-4101 so that I could find the arrangement again.

OPTIONS
Option A: a staffed appointment. The user prefers this option because a member of staff can help them check the change.
Option B: an online form. This remains an alternative; ask the service about its availability.

VOCABULARY IN CONTEXT
The office keeps a record of the contact details.

PRACTICE GLOSSARY (alphabetical)
available — free or ready to be used
record — information kept about a person or event
session — a period of time used for a particular activity
support — help given to someone

REPORT: INFORMATION SESSION

1. Purpose
The fictional Park Learning Centre is comparing ways for people to update their contact details. The case below concerns one user; it does not describe every user.

2. Case and arrangements
The user says: 'My address has changed.' The user has a session on Monday 11 January 2027 at 11:30, in Room 3. Their reference is BE-4201. OPTIONS
Option A: a staffed appointment. The user prefers this option because a member of staff can help them check the change.
Option B: an online form. This remains an alternative; ask the service about its availability.

3. Evidence
In a fictional trial, 18 of 24 people completed a booking. Six did not. Only 12 of the 18 who completed a booking returned a feedback form. Nine of those 12 said the instructions were clear. The report does not record why the six people could not complete a booking.

4. Recommendation
The coordinator believes the trial is promising, but the sample is small. The service should ask people who did not complete a booking about the barriers they experienced before deciding whether the arrangements should continue.

5. Procedure
INSTRUCTIONS
1. First, read your confirmation.
2. Then bring your reference card to Room 3.
3. Check your details before leaving.
If you cannot attend on Monday 11 January 2027, contact Amina before Sunday 10 January 2027 at 18:00. Do not wait until after the session.

VOCABULARY IN CONTEXT
The office keeps a record of the contact details.

PRACTICE GLOSSARY (alphabetical)
available — free or ready to be used
record — information kept about a person or event
session — a period of time used for a particular activity
support — help given to someone

title: Personal information · Language features and meaning
learn: Pronouns link to earlier nouns; connectives show cause, contrast or result. Although signals a contrast, while therefore signals a consequence. Identify what a linking word connects, then explain how changing it would change the meaning.
guided_practice: Use the first checked task to practise the rule or strategy. Read its explanation, correct an error and explain why the answer fits. For the productive tasks, compare your response with the example and rubric before revising.
key_language: record, reference card, because, confirm, support
learner_material:
INSTRUCTIONS
1. First, read your confirmation.
2. Then bring your reference card to Room 4.
3. Check your details before leaving.
If you cannot attend on Monday 18 January 2027, contact Amina before Sunday 17 January 2027 at 18:00. Do not wait until after the session.

EMAIL
Dear Amina,

My address has changed. I would like to update my contact details. Please confirm the session on Monday 18 January 2027 at 12:30, in Room 4. I will bring my reference card. Is there anything else I should prepare?

Kind regards,
Alex Morgan

VOCABULARY IN CONTEXT
The office keeps a record of the contact details.

PRACTICE GLOSSARY (alphabetical)
available — free or ready to be used
record — information kept about a person or event
session — a period of time used for a particular activity
support — help given to someone

tasks.prompt: In the instruction “If you cannot attend”, what does if introduce?
tasks.answer: A condition.
options: An alphabetical list.
A condition.
A completed event in the past.
tasks.explanation: If introduces the situation in which the following instruction applies.

tasks.prompt: Which time belongs to this case?
tasks.explanation: Use the complete date/time detail for this case.

learner_material:
Lina: The session is on Tuesday 02 February 2027 at 14:30. Please listen to the time carefully.
Alex: Did you say 14:30? Thank you. I will write it down.
Lina: Listen and repeat: I can come. I cannot come. Make the difference clear.
Alex: I looked at two classes yesterday. The weekday class clashed with work, so I asked about a Saturday place. I am checking the new arrangement now so that I can prepare for the next visit.

the price of a ticket

tasks.answer: MA
options: MA
tion
Every part equally.

tasks.prompt: Rehearse the session time and one useful word with clear stress and pauses. At higher levels, explain the past event and the present plan using appropriate tenses.

tasks.model: Add relevant detail rather than repeating your first reply. Explain how the weekday class could be considered and ask whether it would meet the stated need. A partner can use the rubric to give feedback.

tasks.prompt: Independent practice: rehearse with a partner, or pause after each partner prompt and answer aloud. Record or note one change to your stress, clarity, register or turn-taking.
tasks.model: Review whether you listened to the prompt, answered it, made your meaning clear and helped establish a next step. Typed notes alone do not demonstrate spoken performance.

REPORT: INFORMATION SESSION

1. Purpose
The fictional Park Learning Centre is comparing ways for people to update their contact details. The case below concerns one user; it does not describe every user.

2. Case and arrangements
The user says: 'My address has changed.' The user has a session on Monday 01 February 2027 at 14:30, in Room 6. Their reference is BE-4501. OPTIONS
Option A: a staffed appointment. The user prefers this option because a member of staff can help them check the change.
Option B: an online form. This remains an alternative; ask the service about its availability.

3. Evidence
In a fictional trial, 18 of 24 people completed a booking. Six did not. Only 12 of the 18 who completed a booking returned a feedback form. Nine of those 12 said the instructions were clear. The report does not record why the six people could not complete a booking.

4. Recommendation
The coordinator believes the trial is promising, but the sample is small. The service should ask people who did not complete a booking about the barriers they experienced before deciding whether the arrangements should continue.

5. Procedure
INSTRUCTIONS
1. First, read your confirmation.
2. Then bring your reference card to Room 6.
3. Check your details before leaving.
If you cannot attend on Monday 01 February 2027, contact Amina before Sunday 31 January 2027 at 18:00. Do not wait until after the session.

VOCABULARY IN CONTEXT
The office keeps a record of the contact details.

PRACTICE GLOSSARY (alphabetical)
available — free or ready to be used
record — information kept about a person or event
session — a period of time used for a particular activity
support — help given to someone

1. Purpose
The fictional Riverside Reception is comparing ways for people to confirm their appointment. The case below concerns one user; it does not describe every user.

2. Case and arrangements
The user says: 'The contact number on my letter is wrong.' The user has a session on Wednesday 03 February 2027 at 9:30, in Room 8. Their reference is BE-4503. OPTIONS
Option A: a reception visit. The user prefers this option because the receptionist can check the letter with them.
Option B: a telephone call. This remains an alternative; ask the service about its availability.

3. Evidence
In a fictional trial, 18 of 24 people completed a booking. Six did not. Only 12 of the 18 who completed a booking returned a feedback form. Nine of those 12 said the instructions were clear. The report does not record why the six people could not complete a booking.

4. Recommendation
The coordinator believes the trial is promising, but the sample is small. The service should ask people who did not complete a booking about the barriers they experienced before deciding whether the arrangements should continue.

5. Procedure
INSTRUCTIONS
1. First, read your confirmation.
2. Then bring your appointment letter to Room 8.
3. Check your details before leaving.
If you cannot attend on Wednesday 03 February 2027, contact Sara before Tuesday 02 February 2027 at 18:00. Do not wait until after the session.

PRACTICE GLOSSARY
available — free or ready to be used
confirm — to state that an arrangement or detail is correct
session — a period of time used for a particular activity
support — help given to someone

learner_material:
REPORT: INFORMATION SESSION

1. Purpose
The fictional Park Learning Centre is comparing ways for people to update their contact details. The case below concerns one user; it does not describe every user.

2. Case and arrangements
The user says: 'My address has changed.' The user has a session on Monday 08 February 2027 at 15:30, in Room 7. Their reference is BE-4601. OPTIONS
Option A: a staffed appointment. The user prefers this option because a member of staff can help them check the change.
Option B: an online form. This remains an alternative; ask the service about its availability.

3. Evidence
In a fictional trial, 18 of 24 people completed a booking. Six did not. Only 12 of the 18 who completed a booking returned a feedback form. Nine of those 12 said the instructions were clear. The report does not record why the six people could not complete a booking.

4. Recommendation
The coordinator believes the trial is promising, but the sample is small. The service should ask people who did not complete a booking about the barriers they experienced before deciding whether the arrangements should continue.

5. Procedure
INSTRUCTIONS
1. First, read your confirmation.
2. Then bring your reference card to Room 7.
3. Check your details before leaving.
If you cannot attend on Monday 08 February 2027, contact Amina before Sunday 07 February 2027 at 18:00. Do not wait until after the session.

VOCABULARY IN CONTEXT
The office keeps a record of the contact details.

PRACTICE GLOSSARY (alphabetical)
available — free or ready to be used
record — information kept about a person or event
session — a period of time used for a particular activity
support — help given to someone

REPORT: REPAIR ADVICE SESSION

1. Purpose
The fictional King Street Housing Office is comparing ways for people to report a window repair. The case below concerns one user; it does not describe every user.

2. Case and arrangements
The user says: 'A window in my flat does not close.' The user has a session on Thursday 11 February 2027 at 11:30, in Room 2. Their reference is BE-4604. OPTIONS
Option A: a telephone report. The user prefers this option because the user can explain the fault and ask what happens next.
Option B: an online report. This remains an alternative; ask the service about its availability.

3. Evidence
In a fictional trial, 18 of 24 people completed a booking. Six did not. Only 12 of the 18 who completed a booking returned a feedback form. Nine of those 12 said the instructions were clear. The report does not record why the six people could not complete a booking.

4. Recommendation
The coordinator believes the trial is promising, but the sample is small. The service should ask people who did not complete a booking about the barriers they experienced before deciding whether the arrangements should continue.

5. Procedure
INSTRUCTIONS
1. First, read your confirmation.
2. Then bring your repair reference to Room 2.
3. Check your details before leaving.
If you cannot attend on Thursday 11 February 2027, contact Ben before Wednesday 10 February 2027 at 18:00. Do not wait until after the session.

CASE DETAILS

Session date: Thursday 11 February 2027
Time: 11:30
Situation: A window in my flat does not close.

The fictional Central Advice Hub is comparing ways for people to get help with an application. The case below concerns one user; it does not describe every user.

2. Case and arrangements
The user says: 'My internet connection is unreliable.' The user has a session on Wednesday 17 February 2027 at 10:30, in Room 8. Their reference is BE-4610. OPTIONS
Option A: an office appointment. The user prefers this option because the user can use a computer and ask for help at the office.
Option B: a video appointment. This remains an alternative; ask the service about its availability.

3. Evidence
In a fictional trial, 18 of 24 people completed a booking. Six did not. Only 12 of the 18 who completed a booking returned a feedback form. Nine of those 12 said the instructions were clear. The report does not record why the six people could not complete a booking.

4. Recommendation
The coordinator believes the trial is promising, but the sample is small. The service should ask people who did not complete a booking about the barriers they experienced before deciding whether the arrangements should continue.

5. Procedure
INSTRUCTIONS
1. First, read your confirmation.
2. Then bring your application number to Room 8.
3. Check your details before leaving.
If you cannot attend on Wednesday 17 February 2027, contact Ali before Tuesday 16 February 2027 at 18:00. Do not wait until after the session.

CASE DETAILS
Reference: BE-4610
Session date: Wednesday 17 February 2027
Time: 10:30
Situation: My internet connection is unreliable.

tasks.model:
REQUEST AND PROPOSED NEXT STEP

Dear Ali,

My internet connection is unreliable. I am writing because I would like to get help with an application. Please confirm the session on Wednesday 17 February 2027 at 10:30, in Room 8.

I have compared an office appointment with a video appointment. I prefer an office appointment because I can use a computer and ask for help at the office. This is a practical choice for my situation; I am not suggesting that everyone would need the same arrangement. I will bring my application number and use reference BE-4610 when I contact the service.

It would be helpful to receive a short written confirmation, particularly if the arrangements change. Although the preferred option appears suitable, I would like to know whether there are any practical restrictions. Clear information would allow me to plan the visit and avoid an unnecessary journey. The service should distinguish a confirmed arrangement from a suggestion so that I know what action to take.

The next step is to check the details and ask any remaining question before the session. If I cannot attend, I will contact the service before Tuesday 16 February 2027 at 18:00. Please let me know whether any further preparation is needed.

REPORT: INFORMATION SESSION

1. Purpose
The fictional Park Learning Centre is comparing ways for people to update their contact details. The case below concerns one user; it does not describe every user.

2. Case and arrangements
The user says: 'My address has changed.' The user has a session on Monday 15 February 2027 at 9:30, in Room 8. Their reference is BE-4701. OPTIONS
Option A: a staffed appointment. The user prefers this option because a member of staff can help them check the change.
Option B: an online form. This remains an alternative; ask the service about its availability.

3. Evidence
In a fictional trial, 18 of 24 people completed a booking. Six did not. Only 12 of the 18 who completed a booking returned a feedback form. Nine of those 12 said the instructions were clear. The report does not record why the six people could not complete a booking.

4. Recommendation
The coordinator believes the trial is promising, but the sample is small. The service should ask people who did not complete a booking about the barriers they experienced before deciding whether the arrangements should continue.

5. Procedure
INSTRUCTIONS
1. First, read your confirmation.
2. Then bring your reference card to Room 8.
3. Check your details before leaving.
If you cannot attend on Monday 15 February 2027, contact Amina before Sunday 14 February 2027 at 18:00. Do not wait until after the session.

SOURCE B: VOLUNTEER LETTER

I welcome choice at Park Learning Centre, but I do not think 9 positive replies prove that all users can get support. We have heard from only half of the 24 people who tried to book. People who did not complete a booking may have different experiences. I recommend keeping both routes during a longer trial and asking those users what prevented them from taking part.

This is the volunteer's interpretation of the same trial figures, not a second independent survey.

VOCABULARY IN CONTEXT
The office keeps a record of the contact details.

PRACTICE GLOSSARY (alphabetical)
available — free or ready to be used
record — information kept about a person or event
session — a period of time used for a particular activity
support — help given to someone

key_language: access, application number, because, confirm, support
learner_material:
REPORT: APPLICATION SUPPORT SESSION

1. Purpose
The fictional Central Advice Hub is comparing ways for people to get help with an application. The case below concerns one user; it does not describe every user.

2. Case and arrangements
The user says: 'My internet connection is unreliable.' The user has a session on Wednesday 24 February 2027 at 11:30, in Room 1. Their reference is BE-4710. OPTIONS
Option A: an office appointment. The user prefers this option because the user can use a computer and ask for help at the office.
Option B: a video appointment. This remains an alternative; ask the service about its availability.

3. Evidence
In a fictional trial, 18 of 24 people completed a booking. Six did not. Only 12 of the 18 who completed a booking returned a feedback form. Nine of those 12 said the instructions were clear. The report does not record why the six people could not complete a booking.

4. Recommendation
The coordinator believes the trial is promising, but the sample is small. The service should ask people who did not complete a booking about the barriers they experienced before deciding whether the arrangements should continue.

5. Procedure
INSTRUCTIONS
1. First, read your confirmation.
2. Then bring your application number to Room 1.
3. Check your details before leaving.
If you cannot attend on Wednesday 24 February 2027, contact Ali before Tuesday 23 February 2027 at 18:00. Do not wait until after the session.

SOURCE B: VOLUNTEER LETTER

I welcome choice at Central Advice Hub, but I do not think 9 positive replies prove that all users can get support. We have heard from only half of the 24 people who tried to book. People who did not complete a booking may have different experiences. I recommend keeping both routes during a longer trial and asking those users what prevented them from taking part.

This is the volunteer's interpretation of the same trial figures, not a second independent survey.

CASE DETAILS
Reference: BE-4710
Session date: Wednesday 24 February 2027
Time: 11:30
Situation: My internet connection is unreliable.
